case_text:
Vignette:
An 18-month-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents with 4 days of profuse watery diarrhea (10-12 episodes daily) and vomiting (6-8 episodes daily). They report he has been increasingly listless and has had no wet diapers in the past 10 hours. He recently started daycare and several children there have been ill with gastroenteritis. On examination, the infant is limp and lethargic with a weak, barely audible cry. Vital signs: T 38.2C, HR 182, RR 32, BP 68/38 (hypotensive for age), capillary refill 5 seconds. The anterior fontanelle is markedly sunken. Eyes appear deeply sunken with absent tears. Mucous membranes are parched. Skin tenting persists for more than 3 seconds when pinched. Weight is 9.8 kg (previous weight at well-child visit 2 weeks ago was 11.2 kg, representing a 12.5% weight loss). Labs: sodium 158 mEq/L, potassium 2.8 mEq/L, BUN 42 mg/dL, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL (elevated for age), bicarbonate 12 mEq/L, glucose 62 mg/dL. IV normal saline bolus 20 mL/kg is initiated.
